requirement:
Habeas Codicem uses a versioned JSON representation of the SDK record: procedure
identity, dependencies, and judgment, together with the application-owned
information needed for requirement, example, citation, and site reviews.

| Information retained | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Recorded subject identity and text, determination, and rationale | Identify the review and its answer. |
| Corrections from a failed requirement or example assessment | Preserve actionable findings under {cite}`requirements.authoring.corrections`. |
| Reference-set digests | Detect changes to the references supporting it. |
| Citation roles and commentary | Preserve the citation's reviewed meaning. |
| Site queries and applicability | Preserve the scope and outcome of a site review. |
| Recorded input information | Check the inputs applicable to that review kind. |

Older negative records without a correction list MUST remain readable.
Correction lists describe findings from the recorded assessment. Loading a record
MUST NOT execute its corrections.

Equivalent information receives the same application validation in both legacy
and versioned records. Versioned fields can live in application-owned output and SDK
dependencies. Outline inputs retain no
source text in the versioned representation.
rationale: Add a test (for example next to `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[failed_definition_corrections_round_trip_and_validate_without_source_access]`, or in `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]`) that stores a failed requirement or example record containing a valid `add_reference` correction (role, file and selector naming an existing project source item). Load it through `HabeasDomain::load_evidence` and through repository inspection, then assert that the referenced source file and the evidence file are byte-for-byte unchanged and that the correction list is returned intact. Also add a round trip of an `add_reference` correction, covering `role`, `file`, `selector` and `rationale`, through `decode` and `encode`. — `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format` says loading a record MUST NOT execute its corrections, and that corrections from a failed assessment are preserved. The only test with a valid correction is `failed_definition_corrections_round_trip_and_validate_without_source_access`. It round-trips one `Manual` correction and never loads through the graph or inspection path, so it never checks for side effects. The `add_reference` entry in that test is an invalid case that only has to fail `decode`. `every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once` and `domain_storage_round_trips_each_review_kind_and_preserves_records_on_errors` use records with no `corrections` field. An implementation could drop or alter the `role`, `file` or `selector` of an `add_reference` correction, or apply it to a source file while loading, and all reviewed tests would still pass. Both are the actionable `add_reference` findings the requirement says to preserve and not execute. The `Manual` variant cannot show either behavior, because it carries no file edit.

Each correction in a `Failed` submission MUST be either
`AddReference { role, file, selector, rationale }` or `Manual { instruction, rationale }`.
An `AddReference` proposes a missing `test` or `impl` reference from an existing
item to the assessed definition. Its file MUST be project-relative and its
selector MUST identify that item. A `Manual` instruction MUST be nonempty and
state what remains to be done.
